3K stays first. Your three real strength sessions stay spread across five calendar days so the quality run and shin tolerance stay protected, while squat, deadlift, and press hold a useful maintenance dose and pull-ups keep one loaded exposure plus one main bodyweight volume exposure each week.

Weeks 2-3 lengthen the Wednesday reps at about your current repeatable split instead of jumping to goal pace. Week 4 trims interval volume for a slightly faster controlled expression. The ruck holds 20 kg and 8 km while pace improves gradually, and pull-ups progress by load, reps, or cleaner execution rather than by adding extra fatigue.

If shin irritation shows up during or within 24 hours of the Wednesday intervals, first repeat or reduce that interval step by 1 rep before cutting the easy runs. If it shows up after the ruck, hold the newest ruck pace target and repeat the last symptom-free week. Use flat road or treadmill for the Run rows if needed, and keep the Backpack Carry as brisk walking only.

Weekly running volume anchor: your established, tolerated baseline is about 18-20 km per week across 3 running exposures, and this block keeps 3 running exposures while quality becomes more 3K-specific. Counting easy runs, warm-up, repetitions and cooldown, Week 1 projects roughly 13.9 km, which is deliberately below that baseline while the new interval specificity is the only impact variable stepping up. While shins and next-day soreness stay normal, rebuild toward the top of your 18-20 km range by adding a few minutes to the easy runs first, never by adding a fourth running day or by making the easy runs faster. If shin symptoms return, reduce the stressor that provoked them or the one most recently increased, the interval session if symptoms follow that session, the ruck if they follow loaded carrying, and easy-run volume only for diffuse accumulated soreness, then repeat the last symptom-free week before progressing again.
